Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - ShopWell SLOs & sizing

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the call today - that was helpful. To recap our main SLOs and what we need from a dedicated capacity evaluation:

- P95 latency for chat-style prompts: ≤ 150ms (token-streaming enabled)
- Sustained throughput: ~300 requests/sec (each request typically ~60 tokens in + 120 tokens out)
- Concurrent active sessions: up to 50 during peak windows
- Streaming: we need token-by-token streaming to our clients (low-latency tail behavior matters)
- Data handling: customer data must be isolated (Dedicated deployment)

Can you confirm whether those targets are achievable on Redwood Dedicated and what GPU sizing you recommend for a PoC? We're looking to run a two-week performance validation with reserved throughput and a short spike test.

Attachments: I can share our synthetic trace if helpful - Tom can provide the export.

Next steps: Can you send a short proposal with GPU comparisons (A100/H100/L4), target reserved throughput, and an estimate for the PoC start date?

Thanks,
Elaine

Hi Elaine - great to sync yesterday. Appreciate the clear SLOs. High-level answers below and a proposed next step to run a short validation PoC. Detailed sizing attached (redwood_dedicated-sizing.pdf).

Short answers:
- Achievable: Yes, based on similar profiles we can meet p95 ≤ 150ms with token streaming when using H100-80GB or A100-80GB at the right config. L4 is more cost-efficient but will need more instances and careful batching to hit p95 at scale.
- Throughput / concurrency: For your profile (~180 tokens per request total), a single H100 (1x80GB) can sustainably serve ~120-160 req/s at p95 150ms with continuous batching and prefix caching. To reach 300 req/s sustained, we'd recommend reserved capacity of 2xH100 or 3xA100 depending on target oversubscription and headroom for spikes.
- Streaming: We support token-by-token streaming in Dedicated; tail latency is influenced by batch window and kernel selection. We'll keep batch windows small (1-5ms) for chat scenarios.
- PoC plan: 2-week window: week 1 functional + baseline microbenchmarks; week 2 sustained soak and spike/chaos tests. We'll provide a reserved throughput SLA for the PoC.

GPU comparison (summary from attached):
- H100 (best perf): lowest p95/tail, fewer instances, higher hourly cost. Best for tight latency SLOs with large model configs.
- A100 (balanced): good middle ground; more predictable performance on existing kernels. Slightly more instances required vs H100 for same SLO.
- L4 (cost-optimized): suitable if you accept slightly higher p95 or increase instances. Good for embedding-heavy or non-tight-latency workloads.

Sizing recommendation for PoC (preliminary):
- Option A (latency-first): 2x H100 (reserved) + 1x H100 for burst (can be hot standby) - estimate sustained 300 req/s with p95 ~120ms.
- Option B (cost-balanced): 3x A100 (reserved) - estimate sustained 300 req/s with p95 ~140-170ms depending on batch tuning.
- Option C (cost-min): 6x L4 - might achieve throughput but p95 likely >200ms unless aggressive tuning/caching.

What we need from you to firm up the sizing:
1) Typical request/response token distribution (you gave averages, but send histogram if available).
2) Example prompt shapes and any heavy system prompts that lengthen sequences.
3) Peak concurrency windows (minutes of peak).
4) Any corporate constraints around model variants (quantized vs fp16) or allowed kernels.

I attached redwood_dedicated-sizing.pdf with more assumptions and a cost estimate. If it's OK, I can loop in Aditya and run a small benchmark with your synthetic trace (shopwell_perf_results.csv) next week.

Proposed next steps:
- You share the synthetic trace and any sample prompts (Tom)
- We schedule a quick alignment call Wed/Thu to confirm PoC metrics and start date
- Redwood runs a 2-day microbenchmark on requested GPU config, then we confirm final PoC sizing and go to a 2-week soak

If that sounds right I can put together a formal statement of work and reserve capacity slots.

Best,
Alex Martinez
